advice.reasonable: Reasonable profit — but watch these risks

advice.lossBody: Your projected costs ({cost}) are higher than projected revenue ({revenue}). Before investing, check each major cost, confirm realistic yield assumptions, verify the current selling price with buyers and test the enterprise at a manageable scale.
advice.thinBody: An ROI of {roi}% leaves a narrow safety margin. A modest fall in selling price, yield or survival can remove the projected profit. Reduce avoidable costs, improve production efficiency and secure buyers before scaling.
advice.reasonableBody: An ROI of {roi}% indicates a potentially workable margin if your production assumptions hold. Protect it by confirming input prices, monitoring yield closely, reducing post-harvest losses and checking the market before harvest.
advice.strongBody: An ROI of {roi}% produces a strong projected return under the current assumptions, but the calculator is a planning tool rather than a guarantee. Confirm costs and selling prices locally, secure a realistic market and keep production records so the result can be tested against actual performance.
advice.breakEvenBody: Your break-even selling price is {price}. The reference low-end market price is around {low} for {commodity}. Keep a safety margin: control production costs, improve quality and avoid relying on a single buyer.
advice.tipTomatoBody: Tomato prices can change sharply by season and location. Plan irrigation and disease management carefully, harvest at the right maturity, reduce handling losses and identify buyers before peak harvest so more of your crop reaches the market in saleable condition.
advice.tipCucumberBody: Use trellising or staking where practical to keep fruits clean, improve airflow and make harvesting easier. Because cucumber is highly perishable, plan regular harvesting and arrange nearby buyers such as retailers, restaurants and hotels before production peaks.
advice.tipCassavaBody: Yield is strongly affected by planting material, weed control and soil fertility during early growth. Use healthy stems, establish the crop quickly, control weeds early and consider processing or reliable bulk buyers so higher yield can translate into better returns.
advice.tipMaizeBody: Profit depends on yield, input costs and the price available at harvest. Use quality seed suited to your environment, manage weeds and nutrients early, monitor pests and plan safe drying and storage so you are not forced to sell immediately when prices are weak.
advice.tipRiceBody: Rice profitability depends on field management, harvest losses, drying, milling quality and market access. Plan water and nutrient management early, harvest at the appropriate moisture level and arrange drying, milling and buyers before the crop is ready.
advice.tipHabaneroBody: Pepper can generate strong returns but prices and quality vary quickly. Use healthy seedlings, maintain steady irrigation and pest management, harvest frequently and handle fruits carefully. Identify buyers and packaging requirements before peak harvest.
advice.tipBroilerBody: Feed is usually the largest broiler cost, so monitor feed intake, growth and mortality every day. Start with reliable chicks, maintain ventilation and biosecurity, control heat and water access, and schedule buyers before birds reach market weight.
advice.tipLayerBody: Layer profitability depends on feed efficiency, flock health and consistent egg sales. Record daily feed use, egg production and mortality, maintain clean water and housing, and build dependable buyers so production is not disrupted by weak market access.
advice.tipFishBody: Feed efficiency and water quality are central to fish profitability. Avoid overfeeding, monitor dissolved oxygen and water condition, grade fish when appropriate and arrange buyers before harvest. Good records help identify when growth or feed conversion begins to deteriorate.
advice.tipPigBody: Feed, health and biosecurity drive pig production costs. Maintain strict hygiene, monitor growth and feed intake, prevent disease introduction and plan sales around market demand. Use reliable records before replacing commercial feed with alternative ingredients.
advice.tipCattleBody: Cattle fattening margins depend heavily on purchase price, weight gain, feed cost and selling timing. Buy healthy animals, assess body condition carefully, control feed waste, provide adequate water and plan the sale before costs begin to erode the expected margin.
advice.tipGoatBody: Goat profitability is strongly influenced by purchase price, health and timing of sale. Select healthy animals, provide adequate nutrition and parasite control, keep records of growth and target periods of strong demand rather than relying only on a high seasonal price.
advice.costControlBody: Review the biggest cost lines first. Your current modeled investment is {cost}. Compare seed, feed, fertilizer, labour, irrigation, transport and post-harvest costs with local quotes, then reduce avoidable costs without sacrificing quality.
advice.marketTitle: Build your market plan before production
advice.marketBody: Do not wait until harvest to look for buyers. Check current prices, identify at least two sales channels, confirm quality requirements and estimate transport and packaging costs before committing capital.
advice.breakEvenActionTitle: Use break-even as a decision checkpoint
advice.breakEvenActionBody: Your modeled break-even price is {price}. Compare it with realistic local selling prices and stress-test the plan for a lower price or yield before planting.
advice.recordsTitle: Keep records for the next cycle
advice.recordsBody: Record actual input quantities, labour, dates, yield, selling price, losses and cash received. Compare actual results with this report to improve your next budget.
advice.returnVisitBody: Save this report and return after harvest to compare actual costs, yield, selling price and profit with the estimate. That comparison turns the calculator into a learning tool for future decisions.
